title: Book Three · Chapter 43: Fifteen
story:
On Thursday, Ronan turns fifteen.

He wakes before Mum calls him. For a moment, the room looks exactly the same. His bag is on the chair. His shoes are beside it.

Then Dad comes through the doorway with a small wrapped box.

“For the old man.”

Ronan sits up. “You first.”

Dad laughs and gives him the box. Inside is a dark blue pen. Ronan holds it carefully and tests the weight in his hand.

Mum brings a plain new shirt. She holds it against his shoulders.

“Try this after breakfast.”

“Now?”

“After breakfast. Keep the egg away from it.”

He eats quickly, then puts the shirt on. The sleeves reach his wrists. He turns once near the window so Mum can see the back.

Dad looks at him.

“Still room for the noodles.”

At school, Kai gives him a small paper bag of nuts.

“All there,” Kai says.

Ronan looks inside. “Did you count?”

“No. I didn't eat them.”

“A difficult morning.”

Kai nods seriously. Then his friend calls him toward the front of the room.

Anna arrives just before the bell. She puts a folded card beside Ronan's notebook.

“Happy birthday.”

Inside, she has drawn a wide window with light across the floor. A very crooked door stands beside it.

Below the drawing are the words Happy Birthday, Ronan.

He looks at the door.

“Mine?”

“It has the handle in the right place now.”

He smiles. “You improved it.”

“Only the handle.”

Ronan puts the card safely inside his book. At lunch, he shares the nuts with Anna, Kai, and the other boys and girls near their desk.

Someone asks if he feels older. He looks down at his new sleeves.

“My shirt does.”

That evening, Dad comes home at his usual time. He washes and starts the noodles. Ronan helps press the dough. Mum prepares vegetables and gives them more room at the table.

Some noodles are wide. Some are narrow. This time, Ronan makes three long ones almost the same size.

They eat together in the warm room. Dad asks about the card. Ronan shows both parents the crooked door and tells them about the hall window.

Mum looks at the new shirt's cuff. It is still clean.

“A good first day.”

“There are still noodles left,” Dad says.

Later, Ronan takes out his unfinished letter to Leo. He opens the new pen and makes one clean dark line on spare paper.

He writes his name below it. The first letters are much larger than the last.

He turns the spare paper and tries again.

From the yard, Dad asks if the pen works.

“The pen does. My hand is still learning.”

“Mine too.”

Ronan smiles. He holds the pen a little less tightly. His next line is lighter, and the point moves more easily.

He wants the birthday sentence in Leo's letter to look good. He reads the last line already on that page before he puts the new pen near it.

There is a little ink on one finger. He looks at his clean new cuff, then finds the old cloth beside the wash bowl. The ink stays on his finger for now, away from the shirt.

He sits down again. He knows Leo will look at the words, and probably find another door to laugh at. He starts the next line carefully.

Then he adds a sentence below the running day story.

I am fifteen now. You can still come and eat with us.

He leaves space for more and puts the pen down. Outside, Mum and Dad are talking in the yard. Ronan takes his chair to the open door and joins them.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

turn fifteen＝满十五岁；wrapped＝包好的；wrist＝手腕；improve＝改善、改进。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan这章正式到了几岁？父母和朋友各给了他什么？
2. Anna的卡片呼应了两人的哪次相处？Ronan给Leo的下一封信是否已经寄出？

## 读句子

**The sleeves reach his wrists.**

拆开看：The sleeves / reach / his wrists.

袖子／长到／他的手腕处。
